places.warn: Fifteen census villages named Hadmatiya were found across Rajkot, Morbi, Jamnagar, Devbhumi Dwarka, Amreli, Bhavnagar, Junagadh, Gir Somnath, Sabarkantha and Mahisagar districts. None is in Surendranagar or Anand, so the travel route does not disambiguate it. The Tankara (Morbi district) candidate is the most plausible on geography alone, but that is inference, not evidence. Both Wikipedia articles titled Hadmatiya contradict themselves on district. Do not pin this until a Gujarati primary source names the district. OpenStreetMap holds only three nodes of the name in Gujarat — Hadmatiya in Paddhari taluka, Rajkot district (22.43352, 70.48005), which also has a railway station of that name on the Rajkot–Wankaner line; a Hadmatiya at 24.64183, 72.68557 in the north; and a Hadmatia locality at 20.71343, 70.87421. None of the three is attested as His Hadmatiya, and the census count is far higher than three, so this only narrows where to look next. Research pass 1 found no source naming the district; the three OpenStreetMap candidates remain the only ones. Gujarati-language search in pass 2 surfaced nothing beyond this; the three OpenStreetMap candidates remain the only ones.

places.evidence: Named in the VS 1952 travel entry.

On the evening of Aso Vad Ekam, VS 1952 — 22 October 1896, the day after Sharad Purnima — He composed the Shri Atmasiddhi Shastra, all 142 verses, at a single sitting, at Sobhagbhai's request, with Ambalalbhai holding the lantern. Revisited in VS 1957 (1900–01). This is, by most reckonings, the most significant single location of His life.
places.warn: Wikipedia's Atma Siddhi article cites 31-3-1888. That is the date of the underlying letter to Lalluji Maharaj, not the composition date. Do not conflate them.

places.evidence: Four documented visits: first in VS 1952 (1895–96) for ten days; again in Vaishakh VS 1953 (April–May 1897) staying with Sobhagbhai; a three-month retreat beginning Magshar Sud 2, VS 1955 (Nov/Dec 1898); and a further twelve days later that year. On a giant rock He recited the first gatha of the third chapter of the Uttaradhyayan Sutra and the whole Dravyasangrah to seven monks, and declared the slab Pudhavi Sheela — Siddhsheela, the abode of the liberated.
places.warn: The Viharbhuvan's own history page dates it to VS 1966 (1909–10) and states it was built on the original rock. The rock is a lifetime site; the building over it is not. The paduka, the Sumatinath idol and the paintings are all later installations. Separately, SRMD's 2023 Dharmayatra report names four further Idar sites — Mahakaleshwar, Chandaneshwar and Khokhanath Mahadev and Ramdwar Mandir — as places where He performed spiritual practices, but gives no lifetime detail; these are 2023 portrait installations at claimed sites.

sites.name: Dhaneshwari Bungalow
sites.note: One of only two buildings the Trust calls original; He stayed about a month. Searched again in pass 2 against the Trust's own Nadiad-Uttarsanda page, which names the bungalow and publishes no address for it. Not the Vanshetra pin, which is a different thing. Still not located. Research pass 2, 16 Sep 2026

sites.name: Shrimad Vankshetra Mandir
sites.note: Pass 1 pinned a Google Maps listing named 'Shrimad Rajchandra Mandir, Vanshetra'. Pass 2 corrects what that pin can be said to be: the Trust's Nadiad-Uttarsanda page separates the Vankshetra forest tract from a lake memorial building it places 500 m away, and the listing is one of those two without saying which. It is certainly not the Dhaneshwari Bungalow. Confidence lowered from building to locality accordingly. Research pass 2, 16 Sep 2026
sites.pin: Locality — one of two nearby sites, not resolved between them

sites.name: The small lake and its memorial building
sites.note: The Trust places this 500 m from the Vankshetra site. The pin recorded against the Vankshetra entry may in fact be this building — the two are not distinguished in any source found. Research pass 2, 16 Sep 2026

places.evidence: A month-long stay at Navlakha nu Dehlu with extensive discourses, meditation in the Digambar posture at the Mahadev temple, and frequent visits to the old cremation ground.
places.warn: Kheda district tourism lists the village's principal havelis as Vithalbhai Haveli and Gopaldas Haveli. 'Navlakha nu Dehlu' is the Trust's name and may be a local usage for one of them — worth confirming on the ground before it is used as a map label. A Google Maps listing 'Shrimad Rajchandra Mandir, Vaso' sits at 22.66274, 72.75636, near Ramji Mandir and Ambika Chowk, but nothing in it says which of the seven sites recorded here it is, or whether it is a modern shrine near all of them. Not attached to any of them.
